title: OIG: ICE Electronic Health Record System Fails Detainee Medical Access Standards
excerpt: A DHS OIG audit found that ICE's electronic health record system does not meet contractual requirements for a patient portal, preventing detainees from accessing their own medical records as required by national detention standards.
content:
DHS OIG Report OIG-26-18, published July 23, 2026, audited ICE's electronic health record (eHR) system to determine how well it addressed capability needs for transferring and accessing detainee medical records.

  • The eHR system did not meet the contractual requirement for a patient portal, which ICE's own Performance-Based National Detention Standards require to give detainees access to their medical records upon request.
  • Without the patient portal, detainees leaving ICE custody must submit a paper written request through facility personnel — a multi-step process that can delay or obstruct timely access to medical history.
  • The audit identified systemic failures in the interoperability of medical records across 18 IHSC-staffed facilities serving as many as 186,900 individuals held across 129 detention sites.

The OIG report was published against a backdrop of sharply rising detainee deaths and multiple lawsuits alleging inadequate medical care. Congress mandated the patient portal as part of national detention standards to ensure continuity of care.
